articles.summary:
Masdar has released its 13th Annual Sustainability Report. Its operating projects generated 40.2 terawatt-hours (TWh) of clean electricity in 2025, up 38 percent from 29.2TWh. That output helped avoid 19.5 […]
The post Masdar’s Clean Power Output Hits 40.2TWh in 2025, Up 38% as Portfolio Reaches 66.5GW appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Masdar’s Clean Power Output Hits 40.2TWh in 2025, Up 38% as Portfolio Reaches 66.5GW
- Generation up 38%: Operating projects generated 40.2TWh in 2025, avoiding 19.5 million tonnes of CO2e.
- Capacity up 40%: Capacity in operation or under construction rose to 45.8GW.
- Green bond demand: A US$1 billion green bond drew US$6.6 billion in orders.
Masdar has released its 13th Annual Sustainability Report. Its operating projects generated 40.2 terawatt-hours (TWh) of clean electricity in 2025, up 38 percent from 29.2TWh. That output helped avoid 19.5 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e).
Capacity in operation or under construction rose about 40 percent, from 32 gigawatts (GW) to 45.8GW. A further 20.7GW of secured projects or projects nearing final investment approval took the total portfolio to 66.5GW. “Masdar’s growth reflects the foresight of the UAE’s leadership and the country’s long-term commitment to clean energy. In 2025, our operating projects generated 40.2TWh of clean electricity and avoided 19.5 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions, delivering reliable power and tangible economic and environmental benefits for our partners and communities around the world. As we advance towards 100GW by 2030, our focus is not simply on scale, but on building a stronger, more competitive global energy business that continues to create value for the UAE and our partners worldwide,” said Mohamed Jameel Al Ramahi, Chief Executive Officer of Masdar.
Quick anonymous worklife pollWhat's my daily work emissions burn, or savings?Powered by ESG News
For the first time, the report includes Saeta Yield and TERNA ENERGY, adding assets across Spain, Portugal, Southeastern and Central Europe. Meanwhile, the 476MW Baltic Eagle Offshore Wind Farm in Germany began generating power. Masdar also inaugurated the 250MW Nur Bukhara solar project in Uzbekistan and secured financing for Saudi Arabia’s 2GW Al Sadawi solar project.
In Abu Dhabi, Masdar broke ground on what it calls a world-first gigascale round-the-clock clean energy project. It pairs a 5.2GW solar plant with a 19GWh battery storage system, designed to deliver 1GW of clean power around the clock. The company did not disclose the project’s cost, its completion date or the method behind its avoided-emissions figure.
Green Bond and Ratings
After updating its Green Finance Framework in March, Masdar issued a further US$1 billion green bond in May. Orders reached US$6.6 billion, and international investors bought 85 percent of the bonds. The company also kept ratings of AA- from S&P, A1 from Moody’s and AA- from Fitch.
RELATED ARTICLE: Masdar, Taaleri Open 154MW Serbia Wind Farm
Communities and Workforce
Masdar ran more than 100 community initiatives across eight countries. At the Zarafshan Wind Farm, AI-powered bird detection recorded no fatalities among target species. Women held 30.2 percent of jobs and 20 percent of management roles. The Emiratization rate, or share of UAE nationals, was about 46 percent, excluding international operations.
Why It Matters
Masdar’s 66.5GW portfolio leaves it 33.5GW short of its 100GW goal for 2030. That positions Masdar to fund its 20.7GW of secured projects with further green bonds, provided investor demand holds. If the Abu Dhabi project performs as designed, Masdar could offer round-the-clock clean power to buyers abroad.

articles.title: Deloitte Survey: 70% of Executives Expect Climate Change to Hit Strategy and Operations Within Three Years
articles.summary:
Deloitte Global, the professional services network, surveyed more than 2,100 C-suite leaders across 29 countries for its 2026 C-suite Sustainability Report. The survey found 70% expect climate change to significantly […]
The post Deloitte Survey: 70% of Executives Expect Climate Change to Hit Strategy and Operations Within Three Years appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Deloitte Survey: 70% of Executives Expect Climate Change to Hit Strategy and Operations Within Three Years
- Climate impact expected: 70% of surveyed C-suite leaders expect climate change to significantly impact strategies and operations within three years.
- Investment returns: 77% say sustainability investments deliver greater return on investment (ROI) than other business investments.
- AI still early: 71% report that AI use for sustainability remains in pilot, experimentation or ad hoc stages.
Deloitte Global, the professional services network, surveyed more than 2,100 C-suite leaders across 29 countries for its 2026 C-suite Sustainability Report. The survey found 70% expect climate change to significantly impact their strategies and operations over the next three years. Now in its fifth year, the report examines how companies are operationalizing sustainability to drive measurable business value and resilience.
Deloitte said its findings suggest corporate sustainability has entered a more disciplined phase. Sustainability remains a top priority on the business agenda and ranks among leaders’ top three priorities. But the firm reported a notable shift from broad sustainability ambition to more focused execution embedded across organizations. It also found greater attention to resilience and to technology as an enabler.
Spending has also risen, with 78% of respondents saying they increased sustainability investments in the last year. However, only 47% said they are embedding sustainability considerations throughout their organization. The summary findings do not disclose the survey’s fieldwork dates, sampling method, or a breakdown of results by country or sector.
RELATED ARTICLE: Deloitte Launches Tool to Price Sustainability Value
Who It Affects
- Finance chiefs and investment committees: Deloitte reports greater attention to ROI in sustainability decisions. Its survey found 77% of leaders say sustainability investments deliver greater ROI than other business investments.
- Technology and data leaders: 71% of respondents report that their AI use for sustainability remains in pilot, experimentation or ad hoc stages rather than full deployment.
- Supply chain and procurement heads: Respondents ranked supply chain disruption as the greatest near-term sustainability-related physical risk, making supplier networks the top physical exposure leaders identified.

articles.title: State Bank of Pakistan, WWF Turn Green Taxonomy Into Carbon-Intensity Checks for Textile SMEs
articles.summary:
WWF-Pakistan and the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) have launched the SME Green Transition Toolkit for the Textile Sector. The toolkit aims to help financial institutions support textile small and […]
The post State Bank of Pakistan, WWF Turn Green Taxonomy Into Carbon-Intensity Checks for Textile SMEs appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
State Bank of Pakistan, WWF Turn Green Taxonomy Into Carbon-Intensity Checks for Textile SMEs
- Toolkit launched: WWF-Pakistan and the State Bank of Pakistan released the SME Green Transition Toolkit for the Textile Sector.
- Taxonomy in practice: The toolkit converts Pakistan’s Green Taxonomy into steps for assessing carbon intensity and energy efficiency.
- Bank pilots next: Banks are expected to test the toolkit with textile clients, backed by further guidance and training.
WWF-Pakistan and the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) have launched the SME Green Transition Toolkit for the Textile Sector. The toolkit aims to help financial institutions support textile small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in adopting cleaner, more resource-efficient practices. It translates Pakistan’s Green Taxonomy, a classification of green economic activities, into practical steps for lenders.
WWF-Pakistan developed the toolkit with the SBP’s Small and Medium Enterprises (SME), Housing & Sustainable Finance Department. The steps cover assessing carbon intensity, or emissions per unit of output, and energy efficiency. They also cover identifying green technologies such as solar energy and waste heat recovery. Finally, the toolkit guides users in developing financeable transition plans, supported by an Excel-based tool.
The textile sector contributes about 8.5% of Pakistan’s GDP and employs nearly 40% of its labour force. As sustainability requirements in international markets evolve, access to green finance is becoming more important for the sector’s competitiveness. By linking environmental performance with financing pathways, the initiative aims to help textile SMEs improve resource efficiency and competitiveness. It also aims to contribute to Pakistan’s broader climate and sustainable finance goals.
RELATED ARTICLE: Deutsche Bank and WWF Team to Further Advance Sustainable Finance
The launch brought together representatives from government, financial institutions and development partners. It also included a technical demonstration of the toolkit. Banks are expected to begin piloting it with textile clients, supported by further guidance and training. The SBP and WWF-Pakistan did not name the participating banks, a pilot timeline or the number of SMEs targeted.
Who It Affects
- Banks and financial institutions: Gain a Green Taxonomy-based method, with an Excel tool, to judge whether textile SME transition plans can be financed.
- Textile SMEs: Borrowers seeking green finance from piloting banks face checks on carbon intensity and energy efficiency, and need financeable transition plans.
- Green technology suppliers: Solar energy and waste heat recovery are named as technologies lenders can identify for textile SMEs to adopt.

articles.summary:
The Global Enabling Sustainability Initiative (GeSI) has named a new Board of Directors for the next three-year term. GeSI works to advance sustainability through digital innovation and is marking 25 […]
The post GeSI Elects Etisalat’s Saeed AlZarooni Chairman, With Google and Greensparc Executives in Top Board Roles appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
GeSI Elects Etisalat’s Saeed AlZarooni Chairman, With Google and Greensparc Executives in Top Board Roles
The Global Enabling Sustainability Initiative (GeSI) has named a new Board of Directors for the next three-year term. GeSI works to advance sustainability through digital innovation and is marking 25 years in the field. Saeed AlZarooni, Group Chief Procurement Officer at Etisalat, was elected Chairman. GeSI said the board’s international makeup aims to strengthen partnerships and speed up collective action across the digital economy.
AlZarooni brings more than 32 years of telecommunications and technology leadership and oversees procurement across 20 operating companies. GeSI said his expertise in AI-enabled procurement and supplier ecosystems will feed its work on responsible supply chains and resilience. Adam Elman, Director of Sustainability, EMEA at Google, will serve as Vice-Chair. He has more than 20 years of corporate sustainability experience spanning data centres, supply chains, products and infrastructure.
Samuel Enoka, Founder & CEO of Greensparc, will serve as Treasurer, bringing experience in energy markets, investment, finance and digital infrastructure. Directors representing 13 more organisations join them, including Alibaba, CATL, Globant, IBM, LONGi, NEC and Verizon. The list also covers Huanghe Science and Technology University (HHSTU), the International Telecommunications Union (ITU), SAWACO, SEE Holding, T-Mobile US and Taiwan Mobile. GeSI did not name the individual directors or give a start date for the term.
Why It Matters
For GeSI, the board pairs leaders from information and communications technology (ICT) with expertise in AI, energy, water and education. GeSI says it aims to tackle the ESG risks of digital technologies while scaling up their positive impact. With procurement and finance leaders in its top roles, GeSI could build joint responsible-sourcing programmes across member supply chains, if directors commit company resources.

articles.title: Schneider Electric Joins Lenovo 360 Circle, Offering IT Partners Scope 1 and 2 Baselines and Site Audits
articles.summary:
Lenovo has named Schneider Electric a strategic ally of Lenovo 360 Circle, its global sustainability community for IT channel partners. Under the partnership, announced on 21 September 2026, Schneider Electric […]
The post Schneider Electric Joins Lenovo 360 Circle, Offering IT Partners Scope 1 and 2 Baselines and Site Audits appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Schneider Electric Joins Lenovo 360 Circle, Offering IT Partners Scope 1 and 2 Baselines and Site Audits
- Strategic ally role: Schneider Electric has joined Lenovo 360 Circle, Lenovo’s global sustainability community for IT channel partners.
- Four-stage pathway: Its Decarbonization Champion initiative takes eligible partners from training to an emissions baseline, a roadmap and action.
- Rebate access: Partners that implement eligible Schneider Electric solutions can access rebate opportunities.
Lenovo has named Schneider Electric a strategic ally of Lenovo 360 Circle, its global sustainability community for IT channel partners. Under the partnership, announced on 21 September 2026, Schneider Electric will bring its Decarbonization Champion initiative to the community. Eligible members gain carbon management tools and hands-on support from Schneider Electric Advisory Services specialists. The companies did not disclose financial terms, eligibility criteria or a launch date for the offer.
Sustainability requirements increasingly shape customer decisions, RFPs (requests for proposals) and supply chains, according to Lenovo. As a result, channel partners face growing pressure to show credible progress, but many struggle to know where to start. “Sustainability is no longer only about commitments; it is increasingly influencing market access, customer preference, and business growth,” said Virginie le Barbu, Lenovo’s Executive Director of Global Sustainability for International Markets. “Through Lenovo 360 Circle and our collaboration with Schneider Electric, partners gain practical decarbonization expertise that helps them strengthen their competitiveness and respond to evolving customer expectations.”
Quick anonymous worklife pollWhat's my daily work emissions burn, or savings?Powered by ESG News
The initiative builds on Lenovo 360 Circle’s existing Connect, Learn and Lead journey with a four-stage pathway. Partners first train through Schneider Electric Sustainability School and Lenovo 360 Sustainability Learning Paths. They then use carbon management tools to set a Scope 1 and Scope 2 baseline, covering direct and purchased-energy emissions. Partners completing those two stages earn Schneider Electric Decarbonization Champion recognition.
In the third stage, Schneider Electric specialists provide a remote site audit, a strategy workshop and a jointly developed roadmap. In the fourth, partners implement priority initiatives and track progress, with rebates available on eligible Schneider Electric solutions. The companies describe the pathway as an ongoing cycle of measurement and improvement, not a one-time assessment. “Every partner’s sustainability journey is unique, but the need for action has never been greater,” said Paul Tyrer, Vice President, Global AI Enterprise and Partner Ecosystem, Schneider Electric. “Through the Decarbonization Champion offer, we’re building the momentum needed to address the broader Scope 3 challenge and drive lasting progress across our industry. Now partners can accelerate progress on Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions with tailored guidance and practical roadmaps aligned to their individual needs. The Decarbonization Champions will be recognized as the leading partners in the IT industry who are setting the highest standard for sustainability by turning ambition into measurable impact.”
RELATED ARTICLE: Schneider Electric Expands SME Decarbonization Program With Greenly
Track Record
Lenovo 360 Circle now counts more than 861 partners across 68 markets. Independent ClimateChoice benchmarking has shown measurable progress across participating partners, according to Lenovo. Schneider Electric supported its top 1,000 suppliers in cutting operational emissions by 56 percent between 2021 and 2025. Both companies were also named Champions in Omdia’s global Sustainable Ecosystems Leadership Matrix 2026.
Why It Matters
For Schneider Electric, the ally role places its Advisory Services and carbon tools inside Lenovo’s global partner network. For Lenovo, Schneider Electric’s specialists add site audits and roadmap support to what 360 Circle offers its members. If partners reach the action stage, rebates on eligible Schneider Electric solutions could open a sales route through Lenovo’s IT channel.

articles.title: ECB Finds Euro Zone Oil Dependence Halved as AI and Fiscal Spending Support Growth
articles.summary:
The euro zone economy has proved more resilient to this year’s energy shock than expected, according to European Central Bank (ECB) economists. Lower fossil fuel dependence, artificial intelligence investment and […]
The post ECB Finds Euro Zone Oil Dependence Halved as AI and Fiscal Spending Support Growth appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
ECB Finds Euro Zone Oil Dependence Halved as AI and Fiscal Spending Support Growth
- Lower oil exposure: The euro zone economy is about half as reliant on oil as in the early 1990s, ECB economists estimate.
- Stronger fiscal support: Fiscal stimulus reached 0.5% of GDP, twice the level expected at the end of last year.
- Temporary growth drivers: ECB economists warn that AI investment, global demand and government spending may fade.
The euro zone economy has proved more resilient to this year’s energy shock than expected, according to European Central Bank (ECB) economists. Lower fossil fuel dependence, artificial intelligence investment and stronger government spending have helped sustain growth despite higher oil and gas prices.
Energy Dependence and Economic Resilience
ECB economists Oscar Arce, Gerrit Koester and Beatrice Pierluigi published the assessment in an ECB blog on Wednesday. They estimated that the euro area now relies on oil about half as much as in the early 1990s. This reduction has limited the economic impact of rising energy prices.
The Iran war disrupted energy markets, pushing oil and gas prices higher and renewing inflation concerns. However, the currency bloc has continued expanding, with business surveys showing that economic activity remains positive. Higher renewable and nuclear electricity generation has also weakened the connection between gas prices and electricity costs in several countries.
AI Investment and Fiscal Support
The ECB economists identified AI-related trade as an “important tailwind” for the euro area. Technology-related export orders and sectors linked to AI have outperformed, supporting economic activity during the energy shock.
Government spending has also exceeded earlier expectations. The fiscal impulse reached 0.5% of gross domestic product, twice the level projected at the end of last year. German government spending on defence and infrastructure accounted for much of the additional support.
However, the economists cautioned that several growth drivers could prove temporary. Global demand, fiscal stimulus and AI investment may weaken, particularly if geopolitical tensions intensify or energy markets face further disruption.
Monetary Policy Implications
The findings arrive as the ECB considers further interest rate increases to contain energy-driven inflation. A third rate increase this year is expected in December, following renewed inflation pressures and a global bond selloff.
The ECB assessment identifies reduced oil exposure as a structural source of resilience, alongside shorter-term support from investment and fiscal policy. However, its economists warn that fresh energy disruptions could leave the euro area vulnerable if those temporary sources of growth weaken.
RELATED ARTICLE: ECB Publishes Climate-Related Disclosures Showing Decarbonization Path
Who It Affects
- Euro zone businesses: Lower oil dependence and stronger electricity generation diversity have reduced exposure to energy price shocks in several countries.
- Technology exporters: AI-related investment and trade have supported stronger export orders and activity in AI-linked sectors.
- European policymakers: Energy-led inflation and the possibility of fading fiscal support complicate decisions on further interest rate increases.

articles.title: Google, Voltus Scale Virtual Power Plant Tenfold to 1 GW Across PJM Grid
articles.summary:
Google and Voltus have expanded their agreement to build a 1-gigawatt (GW) virtual power plant across the PJM grid region. A virtual power plant pools many small energy users so […]
The post Google, Voltus Scale Virtual Power Plant Tenfold to 1 GW Across PJM Grid appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Google, Voltus Scale Virtual Power Plant Tenfold to 1 GW Across PJM Grid
- 1 GW target: Google and Voltus will build a 1-gigawatt virtual power plant across the PJM grid region.
- Tenfold expansion: The deal grows a 100-megawatt agreement the companies signed earlier this year.
- Customer payments: Participating businesses and homes earn bill savings and cash payments for cutting energy use at peak times.
Google and Voltus have expanded their agreement to build a 1-gigawatt (GW) virtual power plant across the PJM grid region. A virtual power plant pools many small energy users so they act as one grid resource. The PJM region serves 67 million people across 13 states and Washington, D.C. Google funds the virtual power plant, while Voltus aggregates the capacity that feeds it.
Voltus pools flexible capacity from local businesses and homes, such as smart thermostats, batteries and industrial assets. During peak demand, these assets temporarily reduce energy use to support grid reliability. In return, participating customers receive direct economic benefits, including bill savings and cash payments.
Google ties the initiative to its commitment to actively bring new capacity to local grids. It also says the program will strengthen regional reliability and affordability. However, the companies did not disclose financial terms, a completion timeline or the number of enrolled customers.
What’s New
The new deal builds on a 100-megawatt (MW) agreement the two companies signed earlier this year. At 1 GW, the expanded portfolio is 10 times the size of that first agreement. According to the announcement, it is one of the largest known distributed capacity portfolios deployed by a hyperscaler to date. Hyperscalers are the largest cloud and data-center operators.
RELATED ARTICLE: Google Backs Texas Electric Freight Route
Why It Matters
For Voltus, Google’s funding now covers 1 GW of thermostats, batteries and industrial assets to enroll across PJM. For Google, the program turns its funding into peak-time capacity drawn from existing local businesses and homes. If enrollment reaches 1 GW, Voltus could take this hyperscaler-funded model to other grid regions.

articles.title: [不同来源] Coca-Cola, Nestlé and Danone Drop Cap and Label From ‘100%’ Bottle Claims After BEUC Complaint
articles.summary:
Danone has agreed to change some of its bottled water labelling practices, the European Commission announced. Consumer group BEUC, which brought the complaint, welcomed the move. Danone is the last […]
The post Coca-Cola, Nestlé and Danone Drop Cap and Label From ‘100%’ Bottle Claims After BEUC Complaint appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Coca-Cola, Nestlé and Danone Drop Cap and Label From ‘100%’ Bottle Claims After BEUC Complaint
- Danone joins in: Danone has agreed to change some bottled water labelling practices. It is the last of the three named companies to do so.
- Caps and labels excluded: Coca-Cola, Nestlé and Danone will specify that “100%” recycling claims exclude the cap and the label.
- No closed-loop imagery: The three traders will avoid suggesting a closed recycling loop or overstating plastic bottles’ environmental benefits.
Danone has agreed to change some of its bottled water labelling practices, the European Commission announced. Consumer group BEUC, which brought the complaint, welcomed the move. Danone is the last of the three companies named in the case to commit to changes, after Coca-Cola and then Nestlé.
BEUC and member organisations from 13 countries filed the complaint in November 2023, with support from ClientEarth and ECOS. They reported the claims to the CPC-Network, the EU’s network of consumer protection authorities. National authorities in Hungary and Sweden coordinated the action.
The Commitments
All three traders have now committed to specify that “100%” recycling claims exclude the cap and the label. They have also agreed to avoid giving the impression of a closed recycling loop. In addition, their labels and marketing must not mislead consumers on the environmental benefits of plastic bottles. “It is great news that the three companies flagged by consumer organisations, Danone, Nestlé and Coca-Cola, have now committed to changing their practices to stop misleading consumers about the recyclability of their products. Consumers need to be able to trust companies’ environmental claims. Danone’s decision to clarify, as the other traders, that its ‘100%’ recycling claims apply only to certain parts of the bottle is a good move for consumers who are concerned about of plastics polluting our soils, rivers and oceans,” said Agustín Reyna, Director General of BEUC.
BEUC said it expects the three traders to comply with their commitments. It also called on authorities to take firm action if they do not. Consumer groups will monitor whether the companies roll out the changes, but the announcement did not disclose a deadline for them or penalties for non-compliance.
RELATED ARTICLE: Bobine Raises $14M To Scale Electrified Plastic Recycling Technology
What BEUC Flagged
BEUC argues the claims breach EU rules on unfair commercial practices. It said “100% recyclable” is ambiguous because it depends on collection infrastructure, sorting and recycling processes. According to BEUC, “100% recycled” also misleads because EU law bars recycled material in bottle lids. Labels are rarely recycled either, and virgin, or non-recycled, plastic is often added to bottle bodies.
BEUC also objected to closed loops, green logos and nature images, which it says suggest environmental neutrality. It cites an estimated EU recycling rate for PET bottles of only 55%. Meanwhile, the chance of a bottle becoming a bottle again is around 30%. “Presenting a bottle as 100% recycled or recyclable is simply misleading and must stop, as must the green imagery that suggests that plastic drink bottles have no environmental impact,” said Reyna.
